live.instructions:
Knips is email and SMS marketing for brokers. Each workspace connects to one housing project. Start most conversations with whoami to ground the current user, available workspaces, connected project, timezone, and plan. Use the project's timezone for date ranges unless the user specifies otherwise.
        Tools that read contacts (search-contacts, preview-segment, get-segments, get-campaign-statistics) run real queries against a database shared by every broker. Use them deliberately: one precise call beats several broad ones, run them one at a time rather than in parallel, and reuse results already in the conversation instead of re-fetching. Never page through a whole contact list or loop over many segments, campaigns, or date ranges to compute something yourself. Use the aggregate tools, or tell the user the question is too broad and offer a narrower one or a link into the app via get-links. If a tool returns a rate-limit or timeout error, stop and tell the user; do not retry or work around it. Heavy usage is attributed to the user's account and can get their MCP access suspended, so protecting the platform protects them.
        Users may call campaigns "innlegg" or "posts" — these mean the same thing as a campaign, so use the campaign tools for them and mirror the user's wording instead of saying "campaign".
        Before drafting any campaign, call get-settings to learn the merchant's branding, and reference recent campaigns via semantic-search-campaigns or search-campaigns to match their voice. When unsure of tone, ask.
        When the user asks to create, set up, or build a flow, call get-flow-blueprints first, pick the blueprint closest to the user's intent, and call it again with that blueprint's key to get each send step's full post content. Blueprints are reference patterns, not templates — study how they wire the trigger, filters, timing, and steps, and how their posts are written (subject lines, copy, structure — the posts are what contacts actually receive), then design a flow tailored to the merchant's brand and the user's stated intent and create it with create-flow. The flow starts inactive with no steps — build it out yourself with add-flow-step (delays, filtered sends, posts; send steps auto-create their backing post), fill each send step's post with update-draft-campaign, and share the returned editorUrl — send steps are always created disabled, so the user reviews, enables the send steps, and activates the flow there. Use update-flow to adjust an inactive flow's name, trigger, reenrollment settings, or step order.
        For campaign or flow content that uses imagery, use search-media to find existing assets, or upload-media if the user has shared a new image. Never reference images that have not been uploaded.
        When showing images or videos to the user in chat, NEVER use embed/preview markdown (`![alt](url)` for images, or any inline player markup). Chat clients can't reliably fetch our media URLs, so embeds render broken. Always use a plain markdown link instead: `[filename](publicReadLink)` — the filename is the visible text, the URL is the link target.
        V1 is read-mostly. You can draft and update draft campaigns, create and update segments, create flows (always inactive), update inactive flows, add and edit steps on inactive flows, and upload media. You cannot send, schedule, activate, mutate contacts, change settings, or delete anything. When the user wants to change something not covered by a tool, call get-links to get the direct URL into the Knips app for that action.
        Treat contact personal data (emails, phone numbers, addresses) as sensitive. Prefer aggregate answers over listing individuals.

tools.title: Get current user
tools.description:
Returns the current user, the projects they have access to, and — when projectId is provided — the active project's context (timezone, plan, permissions).
Each entry in workspaces carries the id every other tool takes as projectId — match the project the user names against this list instead of asking them for an id.
Call this at the start of a session to discover available projects, and re-call it with the new projectId whenever the user switches project so the active context stays accurate.

tools.title: Draft campaign
tools.description:
Creates a new draft campaign. Requires canCreatePosts permission.
                        Block IDs, spans, and looks are auto-generated. Use inline markup for text styling: **bold**, *italic*, __underline__, and inline links as [label](url).
                        DO NOT invent image URLs or product details — use upload-media, search-media, or search-products to obtain real assets and product references first.
                        On success the full new campaign is returned (as `campaign`, including its `hash` for follow-up edits) along with an editor url; give the url to the user so they can inspect the draft. Users may refer to campaigns as "posts" or "innlegg" — mirror their wording instead of "campaign".

Personalization tokens — per-recipient values resolved at send time. Write them as plain text in visible-text fields (block text, image descriptions, title, customizedNotification fields). Never put a token inside a url/urlRedirect field or a [label](url) link target — the link would break. Button labels (link, products, and abandonedCart/abandonedCartButton blocks) and image altText take no tokens at all — keep those plain text.
Syntax: {{ path }} or {{ path | default: 'fallback' }}, written exactly in these shapes — single quotes, no {{- -}} hyphens, and default is the only filter that exists. Only contact and contact.data tokens take a default, and always give them one — the value can be missing for a recipient. Example: "Hi {{ contact.first_name | default: 'there' }}!".
Available paths (anything else is rejected):
- contact: contact.name, contact.first_name, contact.last_name, contact.email, contact.phone, contact.city, contact.country
- custom fields: contact.data.<fieldName> — the workspace's exact tokens are in get_settings under personalization.customFieldTokens; field names are case-sensitive, never guess one
- per-recipient links, as plain-text URLs (the footer already includes unsubscribe links — only use these when explicitly wanted): contact.preferences_url, contact.unsubscribe_email_url, contact.unsubscribe_sms_url, post.web_url
- send date: {{ 'now' | date: '%d/%m/%Y' }}, single-quoted exactly like this (codes: %Y %y %m %B %b %d %A %a %H %M %S). If you insert tokens, make sure to tell the user to double-check that they are properly recognized in the editor

- email, phone, name (string — eq, ne, or fuzzy via like / nlike / slike / elike (case-insensitive); list operators (in/nin) are not supported)
- emailMarketingConsent, smsMarketingConsent (enum — in, nin only; value is an array of "subscribed" | "unsubscribed" | "not_subscribed" (e.g. ["subscribed"]))
- emailMarketingCanReceive, smsMarketingCanReceive (bool — eq; combines consent + suppression)
- tags (list — in, nin, nis)
- created (date — signup date; gt, lt, between; supports period notation like "P30D")
- lastActive, lastConversion, birthDate (date — gt, lt, between)
- followsEmail, followsSms, isActive (bool — eq)
- lifeCycle, country, city, address, postalCode, region, referrer (string — eq, ne, in / like)
- score (number — eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le, between)
- most fields also accept is / nis presence checks (is = has a value, nis = empty) — e.g. email is → contacts with an email address
- event-history fields (receivedEmail, openedEmail, clickedEmail, receivedSMS, clickedSMS) use an eventFilter node instead of a plain filter: {type: "eventFilter", field, operator, value} compares how many times the contact performed the event (ge + "1" = at least once, eq + "0" = never). - conditionFilter operators: flowId eq/ne (flow ids from get_flows); text fields (emailSubject, smsText, host, parameters, url) eq/ne/like/nlike/slike/elike
- any other field name is looked up among the workspace's custom fields and per-contact custom properties (exact name match). An unknown or misspelled name returns empty results rather than an error, so double-check spelling when a filter unexpectedly matches nothing.

Returned fields default to: emailMarketingConsent, smsMarketingConsent, tags, country, city, followsEmail, followsSms, created, lastActive. Pass "fields" to override.

tools.title: Add flow step
tools.description: Adds a single step to an inactive flow in the project. Omit index to append at the end; pass index to insert at that position (later steps shift down). A send step (publish_flow_post_to_contact) must be directly preceded by a delay step and can never be first — add the delay first. A send step always auto-creates its empty backing flow post: the result includes its postId and postHash. Fill the post with update_draft_campaign (pass flowId, and postHash as currentHash). Send steps are always created disabled and cannot be enabled through these tools — the user reviews and enables them in the flow editor. Look up the flow and its current steps via get_flow. Requires canCreatePosts permission.

tools.title: Draft campaign
tools.description:
Creates a new draft campaign. Requires canCreatePosts permission.
                        Block IDs, spans, and looks are auto-generated. Use inline markup for text styling: **bold**, *italic*, __underline__, and inline links as [label](url).
                        DO NOT invent image URLs or product details — use upload-media, search-media, or search-products to obtain real assets and product references first.
                        On success the full new campaign is returned (as `campaign`, including its `hash` for follow-up edits) along with an editor url; give the url to the user so they can inspect the draft. Users may refer to campaigns as "posts" or "innlegg" — mirror their wording instead of "campaign".

Personalization tokens — per-recipient values resolved at send time. Write them as plain text in visible-text fields (block text, image descriptions, title, customizedNotification fields). Never put a token inside a url/urlRedirect field or a [label](url) link target — the link would break. Button labels (link, products, and abandonedCart/abandonedCartButton blocks) and image altText take no tokens at all — keep those plain text.
Syntax: {{ path }} or {{ path | default: 'fallback' }}, written exactly in these shapes — single quotes, no {{- -}} hyphens, and default is the only filter that exists. Only contact and contact.data tokens take a default, and always give them one — the value can be missing for a recipient. Example: "Hi {{ contact.first_name | default: 'there' }}!".
Available paths (anything else is rejected):
- contact: contact.name, contact.first_name, contact.last_name, contact.email, contact.phone, contact.city, contact.country
- custom fields: contact.data.<fieldName> — the workspace's exact tokens are in get_settings under personalization.customFieldTokens; field names are case-sensitive, never guess one
- per-recipient links, as plain-text URLs (the footer already includes unsubscribe links — only use these when explicitly wanted): contact.preferences_url, contact.unsubscribe_email_url, contact.unsubscribe_sms_url, post.web_url
- send date: {{ 'now' | date: '%d/%m/%Y' }}, single-quoted exactly like this (codes: %Y %y %m %B %b %d %A %a %H %M %S). If you insert tokens, make sure to tell the user to double-check that they are properly recognized in the editor

notificationText.description: The SMS text sent when the post is delivered by SMS — a link to the post is appended automatically; falls back to the post text when omitted. Also used as the push notification text. SMS is billed per segment, so each extra segment costs another full message. Keep the text as short as the message allows, ideally one segment, and never beyond smsSettings.maxSegmentLength from get_settings (1 when null): nothing truncates or rejects a longer text, it is sent and billed in full. A single emoji, ellipsis character (…) or accented letter such as á, ê or ç switches the WHOLE text to 70 per segment (67 when multi-part), with each emoji taking two, so write three dots (...) instead. tools.description:
Searches for campaigns on the project. Two mutually-exclusive modes — call with exactly one:

(A) FILTER MODE — exact-match listing. Supply any of: status, channel, publishedAfter, publishedBefore, orderBy, limit, offset. All filters are optional and combined with AND. Use orderBy with one of the allowed enum values (e.g. "publishDate" for "latest campaigns" — NOT "createdAt", which is not a valid column on campaigns).

(B) SEMANTIC MODE — vector search over previously published campaigns ranked by similarity to a natural-language query. Supply only `query` (and optionally `fields`). Returns up to 20 campaigns, most-similar first. Use this when looking for campaigns whose tone, topic, or angle resembles a description — e.g. "warm welcome to new subscribers".

Automated flow campaigns are always excluded in both modes. You MUST provide exactly one mode — passing both `query` and any filter-mode arg is rejected; passing none is rejected. Users may refer to campaigns as "posts" or "innlegg" — mirror their wording instead of "campaign".

- email, phone, name (string — eq, ne, or fuzzy via like / nlike / slike / elike (case-insensitive); list operators (in/nin) are not supported)

- tags (list — in, nin, nis)
- created (date — signup date; gt, lt, between; supports period notation like "P30D")
- lastActive, lastConversion, birthDate (date — gt, lt, between)
- followsEmail, followsSms, isActive (bool — eq)
- lifeCycle, country, city, address, postalCode, region, referrer (string — eq, ne, in / like)
- score (number — eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le, between)

tools.title: Update settings
tools.description:
Updates the project's settings. The settings parameter mirrors what get_settings returns — send only what should change.

Semantics: omitted fields keep their value, and fields equal to the current value produce no write. socialMediaLinks, menuButtons and navigationLinks are replaced wholesale — pass the complete desired value ([] / {} clears). Text sections clear with { isActive: false, text: '' }.

Surface the warnings to the user, get their confirmation, then call again with acknowledgeWarnings=true.

On success the fresh settings are returned; on partial failure errors lists which settings failed and why. Requires hasSettingsAccess permission.

senderName.description: null falls back to the workspace name.

senderEmail.description: Must be on the workspace's verified custom domain; null leaves it unchanged.

smsName.description: Sender name shown on SMS; null falls back to the workspace name.

maxSegmentLength.description: Max SMS segments per message; null leaves it unchanged.

isEnabled.description: Master SMS toggle. Enabling requires an SMS-capable plan; disabling requires no active SMS contacts and resets the default channel to email.

smsSignature.description: Appended to every SMS while active; activating it caps maxSegmentLength at 2. Clear with { isActive: false, text: '' }.

typography.description: Font families are validated against the workspace font list — an unknown family fails with the available ones listed. A set google font wins over the web-safe one.

socialMediaLinks.description: Replaced wholesale — pass the complete desired map; {} removes all links.

menuButtons.description: Replaced wholesale — pass the complete desired list; [] removes all buttons.

id.description: Existing link id from get_settings; omit to create a new link.

navigationLinks.description: The full desired list: entries without id are created, and current links whose id is missing from the list are deleted.

acknowledgeWarnings.description: Set to true to apply the update. Always run once without this flag first and surface the returned warnings to the user for confirmation.

Then call it again with that blueprint's key to also get each send step's full post content (subject, copy, blocks) under `template` — the posts are what contacts actually receive, so study them before designing your own flow with create_flow.

flags.description:
Creates a new draft campaign. Requires canCreatePosts permission.
                        Block IDs, spans, and looks are auto-generated. Use inline markup for text styling: **bold**, *italic*, __underline__, and inline links as [label](url).
                        DO NOT invent image URLs or product details — use upload-media, search-media, or search-products to obtain real assets and product references first.
                        On success the full new campaign is returned (as `campaign`, including its `hash` for follow-up edits) along with an editor url; give the url to the user so they can inspect the draft. Users may refer to campaigns as "posts" or "innlegg" — mirror their wording instead of "campaign".

Personalization tokens — per-recipient values resolved at send time. Write them as plain text in visible-text fields (block text, image descriptions, title, customizedNotification fields). Never put a token inside a url/urlRedirect field or a [label](url) link target — the link would break. Button labels (link, products, and abandonedCart/abandonedCartButton blocks) and image altText take no tokens at all — keep those plain text.
Syntax: {{ path }} or {{ path | default: 'fallback' }}, written exactly in these shapes — single quotes, no {{- -}} hyphens, and default is the only filter that exists. Only contact and contact.data tokens take a default, and always give them one — the value can be missing for a recipient. Example: "Hi {{ contact.first_name | default: 'there' }}!".
Available paths (anything else is rejected):
- contact: contact.name, contact.first_name, contact.last_name, contact.email, contact.phone, contact.city, contact.country
- custom fields: contact.data.<fieldName> — the workspace's exact tokens are in get_settings under personalization.customFieldTokens; field names are case-sensitive, never guess one
- per-recipient links, as plain-text URLs (the footer already includes unsubscribe links — only use these when explicitly wanted): contact.preferences_url, contact.unsubscribe_email_url, contact.unsubscribe_sms_url, post.web_url
- send date: {{ 'now' | date: '%d/%m/%Y' }}, single-quoted exactly like this (codes: %Y %y %m %B %b %d %A %a %H %M %S). If you insert tokens, make sure to tell the user to double-check that they are properly recognized in the editor

flags.description:
Searches for campaigns on the project. Two mutually-exclusive modes — call with exactly one:

(A) FILTER MODE — exact-match listing. Supply any of: status, channel, publishedAfter, publishedBefore, orderBy, limit, offset. All filters are optional and combined with AND. Returns up to 20 campaigns, most-similar first. Use this when looking for campaigns whose tone, topic, or angle resembles a description — e.g. "warm welcome to new subscribers".

Automated flow campaigns are always excluded in both modes. You MUST provide exactly one mode — passing both `query` and any filter-mode arg is rejected; passing none is rejected. Users may refer to campaigns as "posts" or "innlegg" — mirror their wording instead of "campaign".

flags.description:
Search the project's media library across all media types (images, thumbnails, product-pictures, videos).

Filterable fields:
- name (string — filename; eq, ne, like, slike, elike)
- type (string — media type; eq, ne, in, nin; values: "image", "video", "thumbnail", "product-picture", "audio", "document", "application", "other")
- created (date — upload date; gt, lt, between; ISO date strings only (no period notation))
- fileId (uuid — the fileId from earlier results; eq, ne, in, nin)
- postsCount, productsCount, websitesCount (number — how many posts, products or pages use the file ("0" = unused); eq, ne, gt, ge, lt, le, between)
- most fields also accept is / nis presence checks (is = has a value, nis = empty)

Sortable fields: created, name, type.

Returned fields default to: name, type, publicReadLink, thumbnailLink, created. Pass "fields" to override. Every result also includes a `fileId` — pass it as the `fileId` on an image block, a video block, or a media carousel item, to reference that asset (the server fills in the rest).

When showing search results to the user in chat, use a plain markdown link `[name](publicReadLink)` for each item — never an image/video embed (`![](...)` or any inline player markup). Embeds render broken because chat clients can't fetch our storage URLs.
